sections.skill: Prove the converse of the Pythagorean theorem with congruent triangles

questions.skill: Prove the converse of the Pythagorean theorem with congruent triangles
questions.standard_level: High school (Common Core high-school standard; this bank places it at Grade 9 as a first forward step. This is an instructional choice, not an official grade assignment.)
questions.response: write the answer and show the required work
questions.prompt: Triangle ABC has sides BC = a, AC = b, and AB = c, with a² + b² = c². Prove that angle C is a right angle. (Build a right triangle with legs a and b.)
questions.prompt_markup:
Triangle ABC has sides BC = a, AC = b, and AB = c, with a² + b² = c².
Prove that angle C is a right angle. (Build a right triangle with legs a and b.)
questions.required_method: A complete proof: build right triangle DEF with legs EF = a and DF = b and its right angle at F. By the Pythagorean theorem, DE² = a² + b² = c², so DE = c. Then triangles ABC and DEF have all three pairs of sides equal, so they are congruent (SSS), and angle C = angle F = 90°.

questions.skill: Prove the converse of the Pythagorean theorem with congruent triangles
questions.standard_level: High school (Common Core high-school standard; this bank places it at Grade 9 as a first forward step. This is an instructional choice, not an official grade assignment.)
questions.prompt: In that proof, which congruence criterion is used, and why does it apply?
questions.prompt_markup: In that proof, which congruence criterion is used, and why does it apply?
questions.correct_answer: SSS: BC = EF = a, AC = DF = b, and AB = DE = c, so all three pairs of sides are equal.

questions.skill: Use coordinates to show that a triangle is a right triangle
questions.standard_level: High school (Common Core high-school standard; this bank places it at Grade 10 as a second forward step. This is an instructional choice, not an official grade assignment.)
questions.prompt: Is the triangle with vertices (1, 1), (4, 1), and (4, 5) a right triangle? Use side lengths.
questions.prompt_markup: Is the triangle with vertices (1, 1), (4, 1), and (4, 5) a right triangle? Use side lengths.
questions.correct_answer: Yes. The sides are 3, 4, and 5, and 3² + 4² = 5².

questions.domain: Geometry: Expressing Geometric Properties with Equations
questions.skill: Use coordinates to show that a triangle is a right triangle
questions.standard_level: High school (Common Core high-school standard; this bank places it at Grade 10 as a second forward step. This is an instructional choice, not an official grade assignment.)
questions.prompt: Use slopes to decide whether the triangle with vertices (0, 0), (2, 4), and (6, 2) has a right angle at (2, 4).
questions.prompt_markup: Use slopes to decide whether the triangle with vertices (0, 0), (2, 4), and (6, 2) has a right angle at (2, 4).
questions.correct_answer: Yes. The slope from (2, 4) to (0, 0) is 2 and the slope from (2, 4) to (6, 2) is -1/2; their product is -1.
